title: Stop Printing PDFs Just to Sign Them — Fill and Sign Online
description: Printing, signing, and scanning a PDF is a waste of time and paper. Here's how to fill and sign documents online, for free, without an account.
excerpt: Print, sign, scan, email — the most pointless office ritual there is. You can fill and sign a PDF online in two minutes instead.
content:
Someone emails you a form. You print it, sign it by hand, scan it back, and email it. Four steps, a printer, and a scanner — to add one signature. It is one of the most pointless rituals left in office life, and it disappears the moment you fill and sign digitally.

**What "fill and sign" actually means**

Most PDFs that need a signature are not locked; they are just flat documents. You can type directly into the blank fields, add checkmarks, and drop in a signature image or a drawn one — all on screen. No printer, no scanner, no reinstalling desktop software you use twice a year.

**The free workflow**

1. **Open the PDF in a browser tool.** Upload it to [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) — no account, no install.
2. **Type into the fields.** Names, dates, boxes — add text wherever needed.
3. **Add your signature.** Draw it once, or upload a photo of your handwritten signature on white paper.
4. **Export a clean PDF** and email it straight back.

**Why the browser beats the printer**

Besides saving paper and time, a typed-and-signed PDF looks far more professional than a crooked phone scan of a printout. And because [FileTools](https://filetools.eu) processes files in the browser, a sensitive contract does not get uploaded to some company's servers.

**Locked or protected PDFs**

Occasionally a PDF is password-protected or restricted. If it will not let you edit, unlock it first with [FileTools](https://filetools.eu/pdf-unlock), then fill and sign as normal.

The print-sign-scan ritual made sense in 2005. Today it is just friction. Fill and sign on screen, and the form that used to take fifteen minutes takes two.
